newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's TV Azteca says ownership not to split.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's TV Azteca says ownership not to split.

text.p: TV Azteca, Mexico's second largest television broadcaster, on Wednesday denied news reports that its president, Ricardo Salinas Pliego, had split with one of his main partners, Moises Saba.
In a statement, the broadcaster said: "Its totally false that Ricardo Salinas and Moises Saba have broken their relation as partners of TV Azteca."

The split was reported on Wednesday by Reforma newspaper, saying Salinas Pliego and the company's vice-president Jorge Mendoza had met with the head of the Communications and Transport Ministry, Carlos Ruiz Sacristan, to explain the terms of the supposed break-up.
Azteca said neither Salinas Pliego nor Saba had met with Ruiz Sacristan recently.
